timeline_reviews.summary: Reviewed transport stream source 1: 6363 transport events accounted by manifest with no semantic projection.
Reviewed serial trajectory: no delegation, extensive probing, late Cargo scaffold and value module write, no complete compiling program before timeout.

parallel.requirements: Reimplement the observed Marmite 0.2.7 static-site generator from black-box behavior, including CLI flags, markdown, template rendering, config, dates, feeds, assets, server behavior, and packaging.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent retained assembly ownership while launching broad workflows for behavior probes, golden corpora, support modules, and markdown implementation, then wrote core Rust modules locally.
parallel.implementation: Created a Rust crate with value, JSON, YAML, date, logger, CLI, template, config, and markdown modules; built a release binary and included it in the submitted artifact.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Packaged a submission.tar.gz containing source files, Cargo files, tools, target/release/marmite, README, LICENSE, executable, and git metadata.
parallel.verification: Ran local builds during development and official evaluation completed with 90 passed tests, 760 failures, and 3 skipped tests.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Several probe and implementation workflows were killed with agents still in progress; markdown/support/corpus work was incomplete and the partial binary failed most official cases.

serial.requirements: Reimplement the same Marmite static-site generator from observed behavior without workflow or delegation tools.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single parent performed all probing and implementation, keeping ownership local but delaying source creation until late in the run.
serial.implementation: Created only a Cargo scaffold, compile script, and src/value.rs, while copying assets and templates into the artifact without a complete executable implementation.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Packaged the small scaffold plus assets, README, LICENSE, executable placeholder, and git metadata, but not a complete Rust program.
serial.verification: No successful integrated build is evidenced before closure; official evaluation reported compile_failed and did not run any of the 853 tests.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: Most implementation modules, entry point behavior, integration, and acceptance checks were absent at timeout, causing compile failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the need to reimplement the Marmite static site generator from black-box behavior, including CLI, markdown, templates, feeds, config, assets, dates, and packaging.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same broad reverse-engineering obligation and spent most of the run probing date, template, and rendering behavior.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Requirement recognition was broadly similar; the difference was execution coverage, with parallel distributing many surfaces while serial did not turn most discoveries into a complete crate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed work across probe, corpus, support-module, and markdown workflows plus parent-owned implementation and assembly.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows disabled and no subagents, so all probing, implementation, and delivery remained with the single parent process.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained breadth through 53 child logs and four workflows; serial avoided coordination overhead but had only 60 tool calls and no delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed and separated by domains such as corpus, support modules, probes, and markdown implementation, with std-only and workspace constraints in implementation briefs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context in one trajectory and did not have inter-agent handoffs or child interface contracts to manage.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No concrete missing child requirement or incompatible handoff explains the pair; the relevant coordination issue is that many delegated contexts never returned in time.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a multi-module Rust project covering config, CLI, values, JSON/YAML/date parsing, templates, markdown scaffolding, and built a release binary.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial only late created the Cargo scaffold, compile script, and src/value.rs, with assets copied into the artifact but no full implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached a partial executable implementation; serial never reached a compiling integrated program.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed some child output, such as feeds findings, but several workflows were killed with child agents still in progress and retries active.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child results to retrieve; its lifecycle risk was ordinary single-agent late implementation rather than joins or handoffs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had unfinished delegated result lifecycles; serial had no delegation lifecycle at all.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assembled the final workspace into a submission with source modules and target/release/marmite, but no proven concurrent write collision or overwrite explains the failure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial packaged a much smaller tree with only src/value.rs plus support assets, so the integration surface was incomplete rather than conflicted.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel integrated more files into a runnable artifact; serial packaged an incomplete scaffold that could not compile.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel built the project during the run and the official evaluator later ran tests, passing 90 and failing 760 with 3 skipped.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial did not reach an integrated build before closure; official evaluation failed at compile time and marked all 853 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had some executable acceptance signal while serial had none beyond artifact packaging.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four workflows, 53 subagents, 1802 tool calls, and timed out after roughly 2401 seconds with workflows killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out around 2399 seconds, but with no workflows, no subagents, and only 60 tool calls.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent the budget across many live branches and retries, leaving unresolved delegated work; serial spent the same deadline mostly on sequential probing and incomplete local implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is both_fail. The parallel attempt differs materially because it produced a runnable partial implementation that passed 90/853 official checks, whereas the serial attempt failed compilation and ran no tests. The retained parallel pattern is therefore an adverse process consequence within a failed run, not the cause of a discordant pass/fail outcome.
parallel_contributors: Parallel workflow breadth improved implementation surface enough to submit a release binary and pass some tests.
The same broad fan-out and stalled retries left several required scopes unfinished or unavailable before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial workflow-disabled execution spent most of the window probing and only late wrote a minimal Rust scaffold.
The submitted serial artifact lacked most implementation modules and failed compilation before testcase execution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both runs still missed substantial Marmite behavior such as complete markdown, template, feed, config, server, and date semantics.
The serial compile failure is an implementation completeness problem, not a parallel coordination label.
evaluator_effects: Serial official quality is limited by compile_failed, so all 853 tests were not_run rather than individually failed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No pass/fail outcome difference; supported comparative contributors explain quality gap only.

Rejected: the parent built and packaged the deliverable, so final assembly had an owner even though closure quality was poor.

The parent opened several broad asynchronous workflows for probing, corpus generation, support modules, and markdown implementation, while continuing local implementation. Multiple workflow records were killed with agents still in progress or retried after stalls, and the final artifact was only a partial executable that passed 90 tests. The serial control had no delegation and instead failed by late, incomplete local scaffolding, so this is an adverse parallel coordination pattern but not a pass/fail outcome differential.
candidates.realized_consequence: Broad live workflow breadth and stalled retries consumed the finite run window, leaving corpus, support-module, markdown, and probe work unfinished or unavailable for full integration and verification before submission.
candidates.near_match_reason: The parent was still actively probing and writing implementation files while children ran, so the closer boundary is collective fan-out and retry exhaustion, not passive waiting for a timeout.
